question: In July 2018, Europol signed a working arrangement with Israel with the aim of establishing cooperative relations between Europol and Israeli law enforcement authorities. The arrangement does not apply to the transfer of personal data: that would require an international agreement, which is currently being negotiated. The Commission states that it is prepared to continue those negotiations with Israel. 1.

What stage had the negotiations on an agreement on the exchange of personal data with Israel reached by start of the war in Gaza, which has now claimed 40 000 lives, and what meetings had taken place until then?
To what extent has the Commission been prepared to continue negotiations with Israel over the past six months, and to what extent has Israel also been prepared to do so?
What can the Commission say about its plans for further negotiations?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.7.2024) Since their launch in 2021, in the course of four official rounds, considerable progress has been made in the negotiations between the EU and Israel for an agreement on the exchange of personal data between the Εuropean Union Agency for Law Enforcement Cooperation (Europol) and Israel.

Following the fourth negotiation round in September 2022, a draft Agreement text was produced as a result of these negotiations. In the case of Israel, a key requirement of the EU is to ensure that any agreement respects the EU’s consolidated position1 on territorial application by not applying to the geographic areas that came under the administration of the State of Israel after 4 June 1967.

In this respect, following remaining concerns regarding the territorial application provisions of the draft agreement text, as explained by the Commission in the meeting of the Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs of the European Parliament on 5 December 2022, the Commission informed Israel on 2 December 2022 that it is necessary to continue negotiations to find a mutually acceptable agreement.

No further negotiation rounds have been held since then. Considering that its negotiations authorisation from the Council remains valid, the Commission stands ready to continue discussions with Israel at an appropriate moment.
